verses.zh: 那时，又有许多人聚集，并没有甚么吃的。耶稣叫门徒来，说：
verses.en: In those days there was another large crowd with nothing to eat. So[NOTE:1] Jesus[NOTE:2] called his disciples and said to them,
notes: Here καί (kai) has been translated as “so” to indicate the implied sequence of events within the narrative.
Grk “he”; the referent (Jesus) has been specified in the translation for clarity.

verses.zh: 「我怜悯这众人；因为他们同我在这里已经三天，也没有吃的了。
verses.en: “I have compassion on the crowd because they have already been here with me three days, and they have nothing to eat.

verses.zh: 我若打发他们饿着回家，就必在路上困乏，因为其中有从远处来的。」
verses.en: If I send them home hungry, they will faint on the way, and some of them have come from a great distance.”

verses.zh: 门徒回答说：「在这野地，从哪里能得饼，叫这些人吃饱呢？」
verses.en: His disciples answered him, “Where can someone get enough bread in this desolate place to satisfy these people?”

verses.zh: 耶稣问他们说：「你们有多少饼？」他们说：「七个。」
verses.en: He asked them, “How many loaves do you have?” They replied, “Seven.”

verses.zh: 他吩咐众人坐在地上，就拿着这七个饼祝谢了，擘开，递给门徒，叫他们摆开，门徒就摆在众人面前。
verses.en: Then[NOTE:1] he directed the crowd to sit down on the ground. After he took the seven loaves and gave thanks, he broke them and began giving them to the disciples to serve. So[NOTE:2] they served the crowd.
notes: Here καί (kai) has been translated as “then” to indicate the implied sequence of events within the narrative.
Grk “And.” Here καί (kai) has been translated as “so” to indicate the implied result of previous action(s) in the narrative.

verses.zh: 又有几条小鱼；耶稣祝了福，就吩咐也摆在众人面前。
verses.en: They also had a few small fish. After giving thanks for these, he told them to serve these as well.

verses.zh: 众人都吃，并且吃饱了，收拾剩下的零碎，有七筐子。
verses.en: Everyone[NOTE:1] ate and was satisfied, and they picked up the broken pieces left over, seven baskets full.
notes: Grk “They.”

verses.zh: 人数约有四千。耶稣打发他们走了，
verses.en: There were about 4,000[NOTE:1] who ate.[NOTE:2] Then he dismissed them.[NOTE:3]
notes: The parallel in Matt 15:32-39 notes that the 4,000 were only men, a point not made explicit in Mark.
The words “who ate” are not in the Greek text but have been supplied for clarity.

Mark 8:1-10. Many commentators, on the basis of similarities between this account of the feeding of the multitude (8:1-10) and that in 6:30-44, have argued that there is only one event referred to in both passages. While there are similarities in language and in the response of the disciples, there are also noticeable differences, including the different number present on each occasion (i.e., 5,000 in chap. 6 and 4,000 here). In the final analysis, the fact that Jesus refers to two distinct feedings in 8:18-20 settles the issue; this passage represents another very similar incident to that recorded in 6:30-44.

verses.zh: 随即同门徒上船，来到大玛努他境内。
verses.en: Immediately he got into a boat[NOTE:1] with his disciples and went to the district of Dalmanutha.[NOTE:2]
notes: See the note at Mark 1:19 for a description of the first-century fishing boat discovered in 1986 near Tiberias on the western shore of the Sea of Galilee.

The exact location of Dalmanutha is uncertain. It is mentioned nowhere else in the NT. The parallel passage in Matt 15:39 reads either “Magdala” (which is on the western shore of the Sea of Galilee) or “Magadan” (which is the better attested reading but is otherwise unknown). A small anchorage north of Magdala and west of Capernaum investigated in 1970 during a period of low lake levels in the Sea of Galilee has been suggested as the possible location of Dalmanutha (M. Nun, “Ancient Anchorages and Harbors in the Sea of Galilee,” Nature and Land 5 (1971): 212-19) but there is no scholarly consensus.

verses.zh: 法利赛人出来盘问耶稣，求他从天上显个神迹给他们看，想要试探他。
verses.en: Then the Pharisees[NOTE:1] came and began to argue with Jesus, asking for[NOTE:2] a sign from heaven[NOTE:3] to test him.
notes: See the note on Pharisees in 2:16.
Grk “seeking from him.” The participle ζητοῦντες (zētountes) shows the means by which the Pharisees argued with Jesus.
What exactly this sign would have been, given what Jesus was already doing, is not clear. But here is where the fence-sitters reside, refusing to commit to him.

verses.zh: 耶稣心里深深地叹息，说：「这世代为甚么求神迹呢？我实在告诉你们，没有神迹给这世代看。」
verses.en: Sighing deeply in his spirit he said, “Why does this generation look for a sign? I tell you the truth,[NOTE:1] no sign will be given to this generation.”
notes: Grk “Truly (ἀμήν, amēn), I say to you.”

verses.zh: 他就离开他们，又上船往海那边去了。
verses.en: Then[NOTE:1] he left them, got back into the boat, and went to the other side.
notes: Here καί (kai) has been translated as “then” to indicate the implied sequence of events within the narrative.

verses.zh: 门徒忘了带饼；在船上除了一个饼，没有别的食物。
verses.en: Now[NOTE:1] they had forgotten to take bread, except for one loaf they had with them in the boat.
notes: Here καί (kai) has been translated as “now” to indicate the transition to a new topic.

verses.zh: 耶稣嘱咐他们说：「你们要谨慎，防备法利赛人的酵和希律的酵。」
verses.en: And Jesus[NOTE:1] ordered them,[NOTE:2] “Watch out! Beware of the yeast of the Pharisees[NOTE:3] and the yeast of Herod!”
notes: Grk “he”; the referent (Jesus) has been specified in the translation for clarity.
Grk “was giving them orders, saying.” The participle λέγων (legōn) is redundant in English and has not been translated.
See the note on Pharisees in 2:16.

verses.zh: 他们彼此议论说：「这是因为我们没有饼吧。」
verses.en: So they began to discuss with one another about having no bread.[NOTE:1]
notes: Grk “And they were discussing with one another that they had no bread.”

verses.zh: 耶稣看出来，就说：「你们为甚么因为没有饼就议论呢？你们还不省悟，还不明白吗？你们的心还是愚顽吗？
verses.en: When he learned of this,[NOTE:1] Jesus said to them, “Why are you arguing[NOTE:2] about having no bread? Do you still not see or understand? Have your hearts been hardened?
notes: Or “becoming aware of it.”
Or “discussing.”

verses.zh: 你们有眼睛，看不见吗？有耳朵，听不见吗？也不记得吗？
verses.en: Though you have eyes, don’t you see? And though you have ears, can’t you hear?[NOTE:1] Don’t you remember?
notes: Grk “do you not hear?”

verses.zh: 我擘开那五个饼分给五千人，你们收拾的零碎装满了多少篮子呢？」他们说：「十二个。」
verses.en: When I broke the five loaves for the 5,000, how many baskets full of pieces did you pick up?” They replied, “Twelve.”

verses.zh: 「又擘开那七个饼分给四千人，你们收拾的零碎装满了多少筐子呢？」他们说：「七个。」
verses.en: “When I broke the seven loaves for the 4,000, how many baskets full of pieces did you pick up?” They replied,[NOTE:1] “Seven.”
notes: ‡ A difficult textual problem is found here, involving three different variants: καὶ λέγουσιν (kai legousin) is found in א; οἱ δὲ εἶπον (hoi de eipon) is the reading of P45 A D W Θ ƒ1,13 33 M it; and καὶ λέγουσιν αὐτῷ (kai legousin autō) is supported by B C L (Δ 579 892). The first two variants would not be translated differently; the third reading, however, would add “to him” after “they replied.” What complicates the issue is that the external evidence is fairly evenly split between the second and third readings, though the first reading is in agreement with the second reading in lacking the dative pronoun. Indeed, another layout of the problem here could treat this as two distinct problems: καὶ λέγουσιν vs. οἱ δὲ εἶπον and αὐτῷ vs. omission of the word. In this second arrangement of the problem, the reading without the pronoun has slightly stronger support (P45 א A D W Θ ƒ1,13 33 M it). Internally, Mark never elsewhere uses the form εἶπον for the third person plural indicative form of this verb (it is always εἶπαν [eipan]). And although only one other time in Mark is the object lacking after λέγουσιν (6:38), it is a similar context (viz., the disciples’ response before Jesus feeds the 5000). Very tentatively, the reading that is followed here is καὶ λέγουσιν. NA28 puts αὐτῷ in brackets, indicating some doubt as to its authenticity.

verses.zh: 耶稣说：「你们还是不明白吗？」
verses.en: Then[NOTE:1] he said to them, “Do you still not understand?”[NOTE:2]
notes: Here καί (kai) has been translated as “Then” to indicate the implied sequence in the narrative.

Do you still not understand? The disciples in Mark’s Gospel often misunderstood the miracles of Jesus as well as his teaching. Between Matthew, Mark, and Luke, Mark paints the most revealing portrait of the shortcomings of the Twelve (cf. 6:51-52; 7:17-19; 8:1-10, 14-21, 27-30, 33; 9:5, 10, 33; 10:28, 35-45; 14:19, 29-31, 32-37, 50, 66-72).

verses.zh: 他们来到伯赛大，有人带一个瞎子来，求耶稣摸他。
verses.en: Then[NOTE:1] they came to Bethsaida. They brought a blind man to Jesus[NOTE:2] and asked him to touch him.
notes: Here καί (kai) has been translated as “then” to indicate the implied sequence of events within the narrative.
Grk “to him”; the referent (Jesus) has been specified in the translation for clarity.

verses.zh: 耶稣拉着瞎子的手，领他到村外，就吐唾沫在他眼睛上，按手在他身上，问他说：「你看见甚么了？」
verses.en: He took the blind man by the hand and brought him outside of the village. Then[NOTE:1] he spit on his eyes, placed his hands on his eyes[NOTE:2] and asked, “Do you see anything?”
notes: Grk “village, and.” Here καί (kai) has been translated as “then” to indicate the implied sequence of events within the narrative. Because of the length and complexity of the Greek sentence, a new sentence was started here in the translation.
Grk “on him,” but the word πάλιν in v. 25 implies that Jesus touched the man’s eyes at this point.

verses.zh: 他就抬头一看，说：「我看见人了；他们好像树木，并且行走。」
verses.en: Regaining his sight[NOTE:1] he said, “I see people, but they look like trees walking.”
notes: The verb ἀναβλέπω, though normally meaning “look up,” when used in conjunction with blindness means “regain sight.”

verses.zh: 随后又按手在他眼睛上，他定睛一看，就复了原，样样都看得清楚了。
verses.en: Then Jesus[NOTE:1] placed his hands on the man’s[NOTE:2] eyes again. And he opened his eyes,[NOTE:3] his sight was restored, and he saw everything clearly.
notes: Grk “he”; the referent (Jesus) has been specified in the translation for clarity.
Grk “his”; the referent (the blind man) has been specified in the translation for clarity.
Or “he looked intently”; or “he stared with eyes wide open” (BDAG 226 s.v. διαβλέπω 1).

verses.zh: 耶稣打发他回家，说：「连这村子你也不要进去。」
verses.en: Jesus[NOTE:1] sent him home, saying, “Do not even go into the village.”[NOTE:2]
notes: Grk “He”; the referent (Jesus) has been specified in the translation for clarity.

Codex Bezae (D) replaces “Do not even go into the village” with “Go to your house, and do not tell anyone, not even in the village.” Other mss with some minor variations (Θ ƒ13 28 565 2542) expand on this prohibition to read “Go to your house, and if you go into the village, do not tell anyone.” There are several other variants here as well. While these expansions are not part of Mark’s original text, they do accurately reflect the sense of Jesus’ prohibition.

verses.zh: 耶稣和门徒出去，往凯撒利亚•腓立比村庄去；在路上问门徒说：「人说我是谁？」
verses.en: Then Jesus and his disciples went to the villages of Caesarea Philippi.[NOTE:1] On the way he asked his disciples,[NOTE:2] “Who do people say that I am?”
notes: Fpr location see Map1-C1; Map2-F4.
Grk “he asked his disciples, saying to them.” The phrase λέγων αὐτοῖς (legōn autois) is redundant in contemporary English and has not been translated.

verses.zh: 他们说：「有人说是施洗的约翰；有人说是以利亚；又有人说是先知里的一位。」
verses.en: They said,[NOTE:1] “John the Baptist, others say Elijah,[NOTE:2] and still others, one of the prophets.”
notes: Grk “And they said to him, saying.” The participle λέγοντες (legontes) is redundant in contemporary English and has not been translated.
The appearance of Elijah would mean that the end time had come. According to 2 Kgs 2:11, Elijah was still alive. In Mal 4:5 it is said that Elijah would be the precursor of Messiah.

verses.zh: 又问他们说：「你们说我是谁？」彼得回答说：「你是基督。」
verses.en: He asked them, “But who do you say that I am?” Peter answered him,[NOTE:1] “You are the Christ.”[NOTE:2]
notes: Grk “Answering, Peter said to him.” This is redundant in contemporary English and has been simplified to “Peter answered him.”

Or “the Messiah”; both “Christ” (Greek) and “Messiah” (Hebrew and Aramaic) mean “one who has been anointed.”sn The term χριστός (christos) was originally an adjective (“anointed”), developing in LXX into a substantive (“an anointed one”), then developing still further into a technical generic term (“the anointed one”). In the intertestamental period it developed further into a technical term referring to the hoped-for anointed one, that is, a specific individual. In the NT the development starts there (technical-specific), is so used in the gospels, and then develops in Paul to mean virtually Jesus’ last name.

verses.zh: 耶稣就禁戒他们，不要告诉人。
verses.en: Then[NOTE:1] he warned them not to tell anyone about him.[NOTE:2]
notes: Here καί (kai) has been translated as “Then” to indicate the conclusion of the episode.

Mark 8:27-10:52. The entire section 8:27-10:52 is built around three passion predictions of Jesus (8:31; 9:31; 10:33). These predictions form the structure of the section, the content for the section (Jesus’ suffering, death, and the meaning of genuine discipleship) and the mood of the section (i.e., a somber mood). What is interesting is that after each passion prediction, Mark records both the misunderstanding of the disciples and then Jesus’ teaching on the nature of his death and what genuine discipleship is all about: (1) denying oneself (8:34-38); (2) humility and serving (9:33-37); (3) suffering, humble service, and not lording it over people (10:35-45). For further discussion of the structure of the passage, see W. L. Lane, Mark (NICNT), 292-94.

verses.zh: 从此，他教训他们说：「人子必须受许多的苦，被长老、祭司长，和文士弃绝，并且被杀，过三天复活。」
verses.en: Then[NOTE:1] Jesus[NOTE:2] began to teach them that the Son of Man must suffer[NOTE:3] many things and be rejected by the elders, chief priests, and experts in the law,[NOTE:4] and be killed, and after three days rise again.
notes: Here καί (kai) has been translated as “then” to indicate the implied sequence of events within the narrative.
Grk “he”; the referent (Jesus) has been specified in the translation for clarity.
The necessity that the Son of Man suffer is the particular point that needed emphasis, since for many 1st century Jews the Messiah was a glorious and powerful figure, not a suffering one.
Or “and the scribes.” See the note on the phrase “experts in the law” in 1:22.

verses.zh: 耶稣明明地说这话，彼得就拉着他，劝他。
verses.en: He spoke openly about this. So[NOTE:1] Peter took him aside and began to rebuke him.
notes: Here καί (kai) has been translated as “So” to indicate Peter’s rebuke is in response to Jesus’ teaching about the suffering of the Son of Man.

verses.zh: 耶稣转过来，看着门徒，就责备彼得说：「撒但，退我后边去吧！因为你不体贴　神的意思，只体贴人的意思。」
verses.en: But after turning and looking at his disciples, he rebuked Peter and said, “Get behind me, Satan. You are not setting your mind on God’s interests, but on man’s.”[NOTE:1]
notes: Grk “people’s.”

verses.zh: 于是叫众人和门徒来，对他们说：「若有人要跟从我，就当舍己，背起他的十字架来跟从我。
verses.en: Then[NOTE:1] Jesus[NOTE:2] called the crowd, along with his disciples, and said to them, “If anyone wants to become my follower,[NOTE:3] he must deny[NOTE:4] himself, take up his cross,[NOTE:5] and follow me.
notes: Here καί (kai) has been translated as “then” to indicate the implied sequence of events within the narrative.
Grk “he”; the referent (Jesus) has been specified in the translation for clarity.
Grk “to follow after me.”
This translation better expresses the force of the Greek third person imperative than the traditional “let him deny,” which could be understood as merely permissive.
To bear the cross means to accept the rejection of the world for turning to Jesus and following him. Discipleship involves a death that is like a crucifixion; see Gal 6:14.

verses.zh: 因为，凡要救自己生命（或译：灵魂；下同）的，必丧掉生命；凡为我和福音丧掉生命的，必救了生命。
verses.en: For whoever wants to save his life[NOTE:1] will lose it,[NOTE:2] but whoever loses his life because of me and because of the gospel[NOTE:3] will save it.
notes: Grk “soul” (throughout vv. 35-37). The Greek ψυχή (psuchē) has many different meanings depending on the context. The two primary meanings here are the earthly life (animate life, sometimes called “physical life”) and the inner life (the life that transcends the earthly life, sometimes called “the soul”). The fact that the Greek term can have both meanings creates in this verse both a paradox and a wordplay. The desire to preserve both aspects of ψυχή (psuchē) for oneself creates the tension here (cf. BDAG 1099 s.v. 1.a; 2.d,e). Translation of the Greek term ψυχή (psuchē) presents a particularly difficult problem in this verse. Most English versions since the KJV have translated the term “life.” This preserves the paradox of finding one’s “life” (in the sense of earthly life) while at the same time really losing it (in the sense of “soul” or transcendent inner life) and vice versa, but at the same time it obscures the wordplay that results from the same Greek word having multiple meanings. To translate as “soul,” however, gives the modern English reader the impression of the immortal soul at the expense of the earthly life. On the whole it is probably best to use the translation “life” and retain the paradox at the expense of the wordplay.

The Greek word translated life can refer to both earthly, physical life and inner, transcendent life (one’s “soul”). In the context, if a person is not willing to suffer the world’s rejection and persecution in order to follow Jesus but instead seeks to retain his physical life, then that person will lose both physical life and inner, transcendent life (at the judgment). On the other hand, the one who willingly gives up earthly, physical life to follow Jesus (“loses his life because of me and because of the gospel”) will ultimately find one’s “soul” (note that the parallel in John’s Gospel speaks of “guarding one’s ‘soul’ for eternal life” (John 12:25).

Or “for my sake and for the gospel.” The traditional rendering “for my sake” can be understood in the sense of “for my benefit,” but the Greek term ἕνεκα (heneka) indicates the cause or reason for something (BDAG 334 s.v. 1). Here the phrase “because of” was repeated before “the gospel” for clarity and for stylistic reasons.

verses.zh: 人就是赚得全世界，赔上自己的生命，有甚么益处呢？
verses.en: For what benefit is it for a person[NOTE:1] to gain the whole world, yet[NOTE:2] forfeit his life?
notes: Grk “a man,” but ἄνθρωπος (anthrōpos) is used in a generic sense here to refer to both men and women.
Here καί (kai) has been translated as “yet” to indicate the contrast present in this context.

verses.zh: 人还能拿甚么换生命呢？
verses.en: What can a person give in exchange for his life?

verses.zh: 凡在这淫乱罪恶的世代，把我和我的道当作可耻的，人子在他父的荣耀里，同圣天使降临的时候，也要把那人当作可耻的。」
verses.en: For if anyone is ashamed of me and my words in this adulterous and sinful generation, the Son of Man will also be ashamed of him[NOTE:1] when he comes in the glory of his Father with the holy angels.”
notes: How one responds now to Jesus and his teaching is a reflection of how Jesus, as the Son of Man who judges, will respond then in the final judgment.
